lecture_title: Robustness of Anomalies: Data Mining, Multiple Testing, and Out-of-Sample Replication

pages.title: Title
pages.summary: Robustness of anomalies.

pages.title: Roadmap
pages.summary: Overfitting; mitigation ladder; HLZ multiple testing (313 papers, 316 factors); McLean–Pontiff out-of-sample; Hou–Xue–Zhang replication; JKP Bayesian answer; Chen–Welch tradability; value & momentum through the gauntlet.

pages.title: Problems of overfitting
pages.summary: Sample estimates are random variables ⟹ select pure noise, overweight real signals, reject real signals, misallocate. Optimization exaggerates it: weights tilt toward the most estimation error.

pages.title: Selection schematic
pages.summary: No-edge distribution's right tail clears the significance screen (Type I, 'discovered'); real-edge distribution's left tail fails it (Type II, thrown away). More signals tried ⟹ more false positives.

pages.title: Five-step ladder
pages.summary: Diagnostics → robustness → updating → optimization discipline → simulations (rising effort).

pages.title: Diagnostics
pages.summary: Report t-stat, CI on Sharpe, perturbation sensitivity, mountain/drawdown charts, % positive months. Always compare Sharpes over the SAME period.

pages.title: SR confidence interval (normal iid)
pages.summary: SR̂ ~ N(SR, (1/(T−1))(1+SR²/2)); 95% CI = SR̂ ± 2·SE. Ratio of mismeasured variables ⟹ wide. T=120 leaves SE ≈ 0.10 on SR 0.5 (formula convention).

pages.title: SR CI (non-normal)
pages.summary: Var = (1/(T−1))(1 + SR²·kurt/4 − SR·skew). Negative skew and excess kurtosis WIDEN the interval — insurance-sellers have less precise Sharpes.

pages.title: Empirical CIs
pages.summary: Bootstrap (with replacement) vs jackknife (leave-out); jackknife preserves distributional properties better with outliers.

pages.title: Robust measures
pages.summary: % of ±3σ events; fraction of points needed to halve / zero the Sharpe. No excuse for a backtest reporting only a Sharpe.

pages.title: Combating data mining
pages.summary: Track ALL signals tried including rejected; declare ex-ante signs; document stories; adjust Sharpe/t for number tried and correlations. Rejected signals are the denominator of every honest correction.

pages.title: Bonferroni
pages.summary: Per-test p = α/N (Šidák 1−(1−α)^(1/N) agrees); t hurdle = Φ⁻¹(1−0.05/2N): N=1: 1.96, 25: 3.09, 50: 3.28, 100: 3.48, 1000: 4.06. Conservative (assumes independence).

pages.title: F-tests
pages.summary: Joint tests account for covariance between tests — same logic as GRS; why replication papers report joint tests.

pages.title: Robustness tests
pages.summary: Hold-out samples; odd/even month splits (report both); add noise to rankings; drop top 2% positions. A premium is a property of the signal, not of one specification.

pages.title: Post-backtest obligations
pages.summary: Track all signals forward; re-evaluate; combine OOS + backtest strength + a-priori story. A signal's assessment is a time series.

pages.title: Bayesian updating
pages.summary: Quantify prior (theory/academic backing/OOS/longevity), update on backtest, holdout, live: SR_new = w1·prior + w2·backtest + w3·OOS + w4·live.

pages.title: Post-inception tests
pages.summary: Pre- vs post-inception backtest = data-mining bias test; post-inception backtest vs live = implementation drag.

pages.title: Keep track of the dead
pages.summary: Monitor rejected signals (probation) — Type-II error is data mining's opportunity cost; also measures how many things were tried.

pages.title: Optimization discipline
pages.summary: Odd/even optimization, rolling OOS, min/max of CI-based weights. Optimizers chase the largest (noisiest) in-sample mean by construction.

pages.title: Simulations
pages.summary: What Sharpe would N random factors produce? How many random factors to match my backtest? Probable max/min live returns under backtested SR and under its CI.

pages.title: Never full-sample moments
pages.summary: THE rule: never use full-sample moments (especially the mean) — the least visible look-ahead bias. Use odd/even, rolling, other markets.

pages.title: HLZ setup
pages.summary: 313 papers, 316 published factors (an undercount: unpublished and discarded unobservable); overlapping samples ⟹ not independent experiments; 'most claimed findings likely false' (echoing Ioannidis 2005 in medicine).

pages.title: Publication bias
pages.summary: Journals publish new factors, not replications (Critical Finance Review the exception). Published record = right tail of everything tried. Remedies: out-of-sample validation (clean but slow, not real-time) or multiple-testing framework (immediate, needs assumptions).

pages.title: FWER and FDR
pages.summary: FWER = P(≥1 false discovery); FDR = E[false discoveries / discoveries]. Frequentist fixes Type I and minimizes Type II; Bayesian treats them jointly.

pages.title: Bonferroni & Holm
pages.summary: Bonferroni: reject if p(i) ≤ α/M (flat, harshest). Holm step-down: p(i) ≤ α/(M−i+1) (uniformly less conservative, still controls FWER).

pages.title: BHY
pages.summary: Reject if p(i) ≤ (i/M)·α/c(M), c(M)=Σ1/j — controls FDR under arbitrary dependence; linear in rank; step-up.

pages.title: Worked example
pages.summary: HLZ Table 4: M=10, cutoffs 0.5% (Bonf) / 0.60% (Holm) / 0.85% (BHY). Discoveries: single tests 10; Bonferroni 3; Holm 4; BHY 6. Methods diverge at the marginal factor.

pages.title: Thresholds drawn
pages.summary: Flat (Bonferroni), convex (Holm), linear (BHY); at M=316 the Bonferroni p is 0.00016 ⟹ t > 3.7.

pages.title: Factor production
pages.summary: HLZ Fig 2: flat to ~1990 then compounding; 59 new factors in 2010–12 alone; cumulative >240. The t hurdle is a rising function of calendar time.

pages.title: Adjusted t through 2032
pages.summary: HLZ Fig 3: by 2032 Bonferroni ≈4.0, Holm ≈3.8, BHY ≈3.4; HML, MOM, DCG clear even t=4.9.

pages.title: HLZ conclusion
pages.summary: Of 296 significant published factors: 158 false under Bonferroni, 142 under Holm, 132 under BHY(1%) — the conclusion doesn't depend on the method (~20% variation). Limitations: correlations, theory-vs-empirical equal treatment, unconditional tests.

pages.title: MP design
pages.summary: 97 predictors; in-sample vs post-sample vs post-publication separates statistical bias from market learning. Headline: −26% out of sample, −58% post publication; −32% attributable to publication-informed trading.

pages.title: The decay decomposed
pages.summary: Mean monthly returns: 0.582 (in sample, 323 mo) → 0.402 (OOS, 56 mo) → 0.264 (post-pub, 156 mo). First drop = statistical bias; second = arbitrage after people learn.

pages.title: Decay pattern
pages.summary: Decay starts BEFORE publication and deepens for years after. Larger for price/volume-only predictors (weak-form violations) and cheap-to-arbitrage portfolios (liquid, low idiosyncratic risk). 12 of 97 not replicable at all.

pages.title: Volume & short interest
pages.summary: Post-sample → post-publication: trading-volume coefficient 0.092→0.187, short−long short interest 0.166→0.315 (both roughly double, p=0.000); variance unchanged. Sophisticated traders show up after publication.

pages.title: JKP: the two charges
pages.summary: Charge 1 internal validity (HXZ: 'most anomalies fail'); charge 2 external validity (p-hacking; HLZ). JKP: neither tenable — factors replicate, survive joint modeling, hold up OOS, are strengthened by the zoo and by global evidence.

pages.title: Seven bars
pages.summary: 35.0 (HXZ raw) → 55.6 (JKP sample/construction) → 61.3 (drop never-significant claims) → 82.4 (CAPM alphas) → 75.6 (HLZ-style BY adjustment) → 82.4 (Bayesian US) → 82.4 (Bayesian global). HXZ's own MT adjustment takes them 35→18.

pages.title: Construction decomposition
pages.summary: 35→55.6: capped value weights +9.2 (Nokia was 70% of Finland!), 1-month holding +5.0, longer sample +8.3, 15 added factors +0.0, terciles/non-micro breakpoints −6.0, other +4.1.

pages.title: Alphas not raw returns
pages.summary: Theory speaks to risk-adjusted returns; low-beta factors PREDICT negative raw return with positive alpha (BAB) — HXZ's 'failure' is support for the theory. CAPM benchmark: not mechanically linked to the anomalies. 61.3→82.4, still pure OLS.

pages.title: Thirteen themes
pages.summary: Hierarchical clustering of 153 factors: Accruals*, Debt Issuance*, Investment*, Leverage*, Low Risk, Momentum, Profit Growth, Profitability, Quality, Seasonality, Size*, Skewness*, Value (star = bets against characteristic). Within-cluster correlations: Value 0.81 … Seasonality 0.04. The zoo = decentralized refinement, not fraud.

pages.title: Size distribution
pages.summary: EB replication by cap: Mega 77.3, Large 79.8, Small 85.7, Micro 85.7, Nano 68.1 (vs all 82.4). The micro-cap objection fails.

pages.title: Theme by theme
pages.summary: 11 of 13 themes ≥50%; exceptions size (theory says premium ≈ trading-cost differences — strong exactly in EM/micro) and low leverage (CAPM-alpha-insignificant but a top tangency theme).

pages.title: Global replication
pages.summary: OLS/BY/EB-Region/EB-All: US 82.4/75.6/82.4/81.5; Dev ex-US 60.5/31.1/58.0/80.7; Emerging 56.3/37.0/60.5/79.8. BY devastates short samples; EB-All uses only incremental global information.

pages.title: US vs world
pages.summary: world alpha = 0.079 + 0.67×US alpha, R²=0.37 — same-size point estimates, shorter samples abroad; external validity across countries; no publication bias possible.

pages.title: IS vs OOS slopes
pages.summary: GLS slopes 0.57/0.26/0.35 (t 5.29/3.47/4.79), positive intercepts: pure alpha-hacking (slope 0, negative intercept) rejected. But Bayesian no-hacking benchmark ≈0.90 slope: strongest alphas partly mined or arbitraged. Avg alpha 0.49→0.26 (−47% vs MP's 58%).

pages.title: Tangency themes
pages.summary: 10 of 13 themes carry significant tangency weight; displaced: profitability, investment, size. Value stronger than standalone (hedges momentum/quality/low-leverage); low leverage jumps from worst CAPM-alpha theme to heavily weighted.

pages.title: Tangency Sharpe over time
pages.summary: 0.13 (market alone) → 0.80 across all factors (0.56 cross-validated); jumps at new themes: accruals 0.43→0.56, seasonality 0.65→0.74.

pages.title: Bayes case
pages.summary: α ~ N(0,τ²): posterior E(α|α̂) = κα̂ with κ = 1/(1+σ²/(τ²T)); Var = κσ²/T. Prior worth σ²/τ² periods of zero alpha. Attenuated OOS alpha is the EXPECTED outcome of learning, not failure. JKP US calibration κ≈0.90.

pages.title: Alpha-hacking (Prop 1)
pages.summary: Hacked returns: E(α|α̂) = −κ0 + κ_hack·α̂ with κ_hack ≤ κ; pure hacking ⟹ slope 0, negative intercept. 10yr backtest + 10yr live beats 20yr backtest (live is hack-free).

pages.title: Hierarchical model (Props 2–4)
pages.summary: α_i = α_o + c_j + s_n + w_i (theme/signal/idiosyncratic; α_o fixed at 0); joint posterior (Ω⁻¹+TΣ⁻¹)⁻¹(...). Ω off-diagonals: τc²+τs² same signal diff region; τc² same cluster; 0 across clusters. Every factor's evidence tightens every posterior.

pages.title: Empirical Bayes
pages.summary: Hyperparameters by marginal likelihood α̂~N(0, Ω+Σ̂/T); US τc=0.35%, τw=0.21%. Zero data ⟹ no discoveries; infinite data ⟹ OLS, no correction. The data set the severity.

pages.title: Bayesian FDR/FWER
pages.summary: Discovery iff posterior t>1.96 (p-null<2.5%). FDR 0.1% [0,1%]; FWER 5.5% (0.8% at t=2.78); expected fraction of true factors 94.0%; replication rate 82.4% (se 2.8%).

pages.title: Simulation
pages.summary: OLS false-discovery up to 25% when alphas tiny; BY fixes it but sacrifices power; EB matches BY's control and eventually beats even OLS on power. EB adapts.

pages.title: Frequentist vs Bayes
pages.summary: BY leaves points, widens intervals (implied t 2.7); EB moves the point toward zero AND narrows the interval by borrowing strength. Berry–Hochberg: FWER procedures pay too much power; no reason to treat false and missed positives asymmetrically in finance.

pages.title: Posterior over time
pages.summary: Posterior alpha ≈0.4%/mo stable since mid-1980s, below OLS throughout; interval 0.16%→0.10% wide. Worked example: κ=1/2 predicts 5%, factor delivers 5%, posterior stays 5% but tightens [0.5,9.5]→[1.3,8.7].

pages.title: Publication bias robustness
pages.summary: Grant HLZ's own count of secret trials: τc 0.35→0.28→0.20 ⟹ replication 82.4→81.5→79.8 — not 18. OOS-only prior: 81.5.

pages.title: Economic benefit
pages.summary: Factors EB keeps but BY rejects earn IR ≈1 (US 0.93/1.00; world ex-US 1.10/1.60); monthly alphas 0.35/0.24/0.27 (t 5.05/5.33/3.66). t=SR√T: SR-0.5 factor tradable after 15 yrs at t=1.96, 31 yrs at 2.78.

pages.title: JKP conclusions
pages.summary: Test alphas; model factors jointly; let data set the correction; report the posterior; publish code/data (jkpfactors.com). Many factors = strength.

pages.title: Chen–Welch design
pages.summary: ~200 anomalies, original sorts; eras through/post 2005; investable universe top 3000 / top 90% cap. Median 48bp/mo through 2005 all stocks → 7bp post-2005 tradable (~1%/yr before costs).

pages.title: The 2×2
pages.summary: Median bp/mo: 48 (99% pos) / 26 (92%) / 19 (80%) / 7 (67%). Era alone −60%; cap filter alone −½; together −85%, roughly multiplicative. Combos: 250–380bp gross → 0–20bp net (Chen–Velikov).

pages.title: Four papers, four answers
pages.summary: HLZ: much is MT noise. MP: −26% bias, −58% post-pub. JKP: largely replicates. CW: replicates but 7bp/mo tradable, median t 0.45 — 'useless to non-micro managers in the 21st century.' Not mutually exclusive. Excluded: factor timing, ML combos, alt data.

pages.title: Under/overfitting
pages.summary: Model vs data tradeoff: simple (first principles, omits variables) vs data-driven (captures signal AND noise). Same for CAPM vs the zoo.

pages.title: Why theory matters
pages.summary: Filters noise (also filters unexplained truths — the price); intuition; peso problem: truth invisible in data, visible in theory. Silly published factors: lunar phases, sports sentiment, temperature.

pages.title: What is a good t-stat?
pages.summary: 1.96 = 5% per-test false-positive chance; says nothing about a literature running hundreds of tests. Suggest ≥3.0 (or 5.0). Simulation: 1000 factors, 100 real: at t=1.95, 143 discoveries, 49 junk. Log-scale: t=2 needs ~400 tests to fluke, t=3 ~8,329... actually: tests to fluke: t 2 ≈ 121?, series: 121/393/8,329/408,234/4.4e11 for t 2/2.5?/3/3.5?/5. EW factor index t>11 ⟹ >1 trillion trials.

pages.title: The handful
pages.summary: Citations (000s): Value 72.1, Size 58.1, Momentum 33.1, Beta 19.4, FSQ 18.3 — ~90% of citations in 4–5 factors; 17 more in a thin tail.

pages.title: Putting it together
pages.summary: Impact-weighted, academia focuses on the robust factors; time wasted on data-mined factors is small; EW factor index t>11.

pages.title: Concluding standout
pages.summary: Most don't matter — a few REALLY do.

pages.title: Summary
pages.summary: Report intervals; keep score of everything tried; MT raises the bar mechanically (1.96→3.28 at 50 tests); decay is real (−26/−32); HXZ: 64% of 447 fail at 5%, 85% at t=3; value & momentum clear all four criteria. The rule: t≥3 + robustness + OOS + story.

pages.title: Value gauntlet
pages.summary: Rosenberg–Reid–Lanstein 1985, FF 1992. Four criteria. Robustness: B/P 3.6, E/P 5.3, CF/P 4.5, D/P 1.8, LT-reversal 2.5, composite 3.5 %/yr (1951–2014) — every construction positive. OOS t-stats: US OOS 3.62, non-US full 4.49, non-US OOS 2.93. Two stories (risk/distress; neglect/extrapolation).

pages.title: Momentum gauntlet
pages.summary: JT 1993. 16 constructions (4 lookbacks × 4 holds, 1965–89): only 3mo/3mo (t 1.10) fails t=2; grid 1.10,2.29,2.69,3.53/2.44,3.07,3.76,3.36/3.03,3.78,3.47,2.89/3.74,3.40,2.95,2.25. OOS: US 2.78, non-US full 4.49, non-US OOS 5.99 — STRONGER out of sample abroad. Two stories (risk: winners' cost of capital; behavioral: underreaction + delayed overreaction). Clears all four.
